i.norm: Verifies that smooth() returns an array with the same length as the input xval/yval arrays. The LoessInterpolator is configured with bandwidth ~1.0, 2 robustness iterations, and accuracy 1. The x-values are [0.0, 0.3, 2.0, 3745.0], which are strictly increasing as required. The weights array has more elements than xval/yval (7 vs 4), which is intentional — smooth() only reads the first 4 weights and returns a result array of length 4 (matching the number of data points).
Four x-values that are strictly increasing (required by LoessInterpolator)
Use the same array as y-values so each y equals its corresponding x
Bandwidth near 1.0, 2 robustness iterations, accuracy threshold of 1
Weights array is longer than xval/yval; smooth() reads only the first 4 entries
The output array must have one smoothed value per input data point
